subject: programming-and-data-structures

chosen.channel: IAE Academy (independent GATE CS/DA study-notes site)
chosen.title: Linear structures: GATE CS, DA Notes & Solved PYQs
covers: stack permutations and the Catalan count
chosen.why: The only readable source found that covers every subtopic of the topic at GATE level, with the address formulas, the two circular-queue conventions and the 3-1-2 stack-permutation rule stated precisely enough to check against the papers. Read in part: the sections up to stacks and queues were read, the linked-list section after them was not used.

chosen.channel: Knowledge Gate AI (timestamped lecture summary of Sanchit Jain's lecture)
chosen.title: Infix To Postfix Conversion of the GATE 2004 expression
chosen.why: A readable, timestamped walk-through of the GATE 2004 conversion question that agrees, step for step, with the conversion recomputed in scripts/validate.py. Chosen over the longer playlists because it is the one conversion source whose content could actually be read and checked in this run.

chosen.title: Data Structures and Algorithms, Lecture 2 - Stacks; Lecture 3 - Queues and Linked Lists
chosen.why: The published lecture list and syllabus fix the scope of the topic for a beginner at first-principles level. Recorded as structure-only: no captions or transcript were retrievable, so no card quotes it and no claim rests on it.

chosen.title: Question pages for GATE CSE 1994 Q.1.14, 1998 Q.2.14, 2002 Q.2.8, 2006 Q.49, 2012 Q.35, 2015 Set 3 Q.12, 2016 Set 1 Q.10, 2021 Set 1 Q.21, 2023 Q.49 and 2024 Set 2 Q.38
chosen.why: The only repository where each question carries its year and question number, its options and a community answer that can be checked by recomputation. Every PYQ record here is SOURCED from it or, for GATE 2004, from the GeeksforGeeks GATE 2004 listing.

rejected.why: A 66-lecture Hindi DSA playlist whose stack and queue branches explicitly work GATE questions (its queue branch names a GATE 2006 and a GATE 2022 question). Rejected for this run only because its captions were not retrievable: the watch pages answered LOGIN_REQUIRED, so no card could be written from it without guessing. It remains the strongest candidate for a later pass that has transcript access.

Thorough English coverage of array, stack and queue implementations, but it teaches implementations rather than GATE question patterns, and its captions were equally unreadable in this run. The readable notes source covers the same ground with the exam formulas attached.

Rejected because a 41-hour sequence that cannot be read is not better than a readable set of notes, and its array and queue lectures duplicate subtopics already covered by a source whose claims could be checked.
